data.title: WLD’s 15% price surge follows World Network’s launch of ‘World Money’ Super App
data.description:
Identity-focused crypto project World Network [WLD] launched World Money, a self-custodial “super app,” on Thursday, 17th September. The app, now available in 150 countries, combines trading, stablecoin payments, and digital asset rewards.

It also allows users to access other mini-apps such as Kalshi, Stripe, Credit, and Morpho. The app supports eight currencies, while Stripe supports a U.S funding flow that allows users to convert money from Apple Pay to stablecoins.

The launch of the World Money app boosted market sentiment and sent WLD’s price soaring by 15%. Open Interest hiked by 8.5% in just 24 hours too. At the time of writing, the spot CVD had begun to recover and push higher, underlining organic demand for the altcoin.

The funding rates were also positive but not overextended, reflecting healthy market conditions on the derivatives side. Can WLD keep the run going?

Deciphering Worldcoin’s price trends

The 1-day chart showed that the higher timeframe price structure was shifting bullishly. The rally from $0.226 to $0.723 in May-June established a trend shift. The deep retracement to $0.30 had ended.

The internal swing point at $0.445 (green) was breached earlier in September. The rally of the past week originated at the $0.353 local support level (orange), a local support zone that was tested in late August too.

The CMF was at +0.07, and the A/D indicator has been climbing higher in recent days. The volume indicators revealed demand was present too.

The DMI suggested that a strong uptrend was in progress on the daily timeframe. This could be another encouraging sign for swing traders and long-term investors.

Traders’ call to action – Stay bullish

The local supply zone around $0.41 was cleared and was also retested as support, confirming its flip to a demand zone. The technical indicators were also bullish on the 2-hour chart.

It is likely that WLD will continue to trend higher, provided Bitcoin [BTC] does not see a major sell-off.

Final Summary

  • Tools for Humanity, co-founded by OpenAI’s Sam Altman, is behind World Money, the financial “super app” that has been in the works since March 2025.
  • The WLD altcoin saw a bullish sentiment shift that fueled its recent price gains.

data.title: Analyzing why Shiba Inu crypto’s latest breakout is somewhat subdued
data.description:
The memecoin market has gained by 5% over the week, compared to Bitcoin’s [BTC] 1.40% and Ethereum’s [ETH] 2.04%. Layer 2 tokens have performed the best though, with 20.7% gains over the same time period.

Dogecoin [DOGE] often sets the direction for the memecoin sector. At press time, it was up 4.50% in 24 hours and up 2.03% over the last 7 days.

What about SHIB though? Well, Shiba Inu [SHIB] has performed slightly better than DOGE. As the second-largest memecoin by market cap, SHIB was up 5.78% in a day and 6.37% in a week.

Hence, the question: How will the memecoin trend for the rest of September?

Shiba Inu’s downtrend might be weakening

On the 1-day chart, the swift decline from May to July marked a bearish swing move for Shiba Inu. Since then, the token has picked up some bullish momentum though.

In recent weeks, the MFI has hovered around neutral-50 for the most part. All while the CMF climbed above +0.05 in late August and early September to show sizeable capital inflows.

The technical indicators showed a potential short-term uptrend, but there’s another reason why swing traders need to be prepared for a bullish trend shift in the higher timeframes.

SHIB tested the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $0.00000613 in August and faced rejection. Since then, the memecoin has defended the $0.00000495 support level twice.

Sellers’ inability to break this short-term support could be a sign of weakness. However, a bullish follow-through will need sustained demand and positive memecoin market sentiment to keep the move going.

Traders’ call to action – Wait

On the 4-hour chart, the $0.0000055 (red) supply zone has been a challenge for Shiba Inu crypto bulls throughout September. A breakout past this supply zone is necessary to shift the short-term bias to bullish.

Though the MFI was close to overbought conditions, the CMF stubbornly remained beneath +0.05. It suggested steady buying pressure was not behind SHIB despite the gains over the past couple of days.

Even if the $0.0000055-area is overcome, the higher timeframe Fibonacci retracement level at $0.00000613 could still stand strong. Therefore, traders can wait for a bullish trend shift on the daily timeframe, or look to sell a SHIB rally into key supply zones.

Final Summary

  • Memecoin market has been able to outperform Bitcoin and Ethereum over the past week.
  • Shiba Inu has made strong gains recently, but is yet to clear the pivotal short-term resistance zone at $0.0000055.

data.title: How did North Korea’s WaterPlum steal crypto worth $10.7M with fake job interviews?
data.description:
North Korea’s threat to the crypto industry is getting bigger by the day. According to a report by Japan’s National Police Agency (NPA) and the U.S Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), North Korean state-backed group WaterPlum stole $10.7M through fake headhunting. 

WaterPlum reportedly posed as hiring managers for crypto firms, NFT businesses, and artificial intelligence companies and reached out to IT and software developers. 

However, through a fake skill test, the victims were duped into downloading malicious programs that drained their wallets. Separately, the group also posed as employees and bagged lucrative offers with crypto firms only to gain access to their systems and compromise them. 

According to the report, the group infiltrated 30K devices across over 100 countries, affecting over 7000 crypto wallets. And, it did this over an eight-month period from December 2025 to July 2026. 

North Korea’s evolving crypto heist strategy

For perspective, WaterPlum is just one of the threat actors backed by North Korea, tracked by most security firms. And, it appears WaterPlum is purely designed for wide-scale fake recruitment schemes to deliver malware and steal victims’ crypto assets. 

However, some of the recent high-value exploits have also been done by state-backed actors from North Korea. For example, TRM Labs linked the $285M Drift protocol hack to AppleJesus, also known as Citrine Sleet or UNC4736. This involved a daring 6-month face-to-face social engineering plan and $1M of their committed capital to compromise the core protocol’s contributors. 

Perhaps one of the most lethal and high-value operators is the Lazarus Group, which is also backed by the state. It was behind the historic $1.5B Bybit exchange heist and KelpDAO’s $292M exploit. 

Overall, these threat actors seem to be so sophisticated and organized, with each group with different targets and ways of compromising them. Interestingly, all the stolen crypto funds have become a crucial state revenue stream for North Korea, according to Certik.

In 2025, North Korean threat actors accounted for 60% or $2B of the $3.4B annual crypto losses, as per Certik. In fact, another security research firm, TRM Labs, estimated that the country drove 64% of overall crypto exploits last year. 

As of H2 2026, North Korea-based hackers have accounted for 76% of total crypto losses, worth over $600M. They’ve marked a steady dominance and been a risk to the industry since 2020. 

Final Summary

  • Japan, the United States, and other countries reported that over $10M have been lost to fake job interviews by WaterPlum. 
  • North Korea now accounts for over 75% of stolen crypto funds in 2026.

data.title: Revolut hackers demand 6,000 XMR as Italy opens data probe
data.description:
Italian prosecutors have opened an investigation after criminals allegedly used a compromised government email account to obtain information about hundreds of Revolut customers.

The group that claimed to be behind it demanded 6,000 Monero [XMR], worth about $3 million. The deadline they set has passed, but it is not known if Revolut paid or not, or if the data has now been sold as they threatened.

Hackers allegedly targeted crypto holders

The ransom demand was unveiled with a 24-hour countdown by the group, which calls itself “iamnotavillain”, on September 16.

According to the Financial Times, the attackers threatened to sell sensitive customer records to criminals if Revolut did not pay.

Several passports, driving licenses, identity photographs, and transaction histories were all visible on screen in a video that the FT watched. At least 680 customer accounts have been compromised.

The attackers said that they identified customers with a lot of crypto holdings by doing blockchain analysis. They said they got the records after they compromised an Italian government email system and acted as if they were law enforcement officials.

Revolut responded by stating they had not formally heard back from the group nor received any ransom demands. They confirmed that none of its internal nor client funds had been affected nor breached.

Revolut has said that they have been working closely with other regulators and law enforcement bodies, and have also offered to help and support any of its affected customers.

Italian prosecutors and the country’s anti-mafia and counterterrorism authorities are now investigating the incident, according to an updated Euronews report.

Why the attackers demanded Monero

Monero hides information that most public blockchains display, including transaction amounts and the identities of senders and recipients.

These protections offer financial privacy to ordinary users. Yet, they also provide an appealing option for criminals seeking to hide ransoms.

This incident implies in no way that the Monero network itself was breached and implicated in obtaining the customers’ records; XMR was employed by the attackers as their chosen method of payment.

XMR was trading near $546 when writing, up by more than 5.7% from opening. XMR jumped above $600 for a few minutes but has dropped from those levels.

​Yet while the price remained above its recent average, the massive wick from $608 showed that sellers were not playing around when the price rose to a certain level.

Final Summary

  • After allegedly leaking the records of at least 680 customers, the attacker[s] demanded payment of 6,000 XMR!
  • Revolut’s systems and customers’ funds were said to still be secure, while it is not clear what happened after the ransom demand time expired.

data.title: Nostra hit by $3.5M Oracle attack as security concerns re-emerge — Details
data.description:
Crypto security took another hit today after Nostra’s lending market on Starknet app was reportedly exploited through manipulation of the price feed for NSTR. The attacker was able to do this by scheming the protocol’s oracle to report an inaccurate NSTR value.

Since Nostra uses that oracle’s price to determine how much collateral is worth, the manipulated price apparently made the attacker’s NSTR collateral look more valuable than it really was.

Funds lost and laundered

Once the manipulated NSTR price was accepted by Nostra’s oracle, the attacker was able to use the overvalued NSTR collateral to borrow roughly $3.5 million in Ethereum [ETH], Starkent [STRK], Circle [USDC], Tether [USDT], Wrapped Bitcoin [WBTC], and DAIv1.

Now since the collateral value and borrowing limits were determined using the wrong price, the loans might have seemed legitimate. This allowed the attacker to move a step ahead and bridge about $1.92 million to Ethereum, comprising of 234.57 ETH and 1.3 million DAI.

However, the $3.5 million borrowed is not the final loss reported by the team. Especially as Nostra is still assessing the impact and potential recoveries.

However, as a safety measure, the protocol has paused lending, borrowing, withdrawals, and liquidations while investigating the oracle manipulation. The exact method is yet to be disclosed too.

More incidents over the past 2 weeks

This episode coincided with a recent attack on Revolut, which fell victim to a sophisticated phishing attack after a fraudulent government request passed its security checks.

Meanwhile, Term Finance was attacked after the wrongdoer exploited weaknesses in its DAO governance. Liquid Network’s hack too saw attackers exploit a software flaw to generate around 4,000 BTC.

All about the growing scam epidemic

Cases like these have pushed crypto security losses in H1 2026 to $1.1 billion across more than 212 on-chain incidents. In fact, April alone accounted for over $600 million, led by the KelpDAO and Drift Protocol exploits.

In these 6 months, Ethereum recorded the highest losses worth $332 million, followed closely by Solana at $326 million.

Over the past year, crypto exploits have already resulted in approximately $2.101 billion in total value hacked. Of this amount, around $1.353 billion was lost in DeFi protocols, while cross-chain bridges accounted for a further $758.96 million in hacked funds.

Final Summary

  • Attacker was able to use the overvalued NSTR collateral to borrow roughly $3.5 million in ETH, STRK, USDC, USDT, WBTC, and DAIv1.
  • About $1.92 million to Ethereum, comprising 234.57 ETH and 1.3 million DAI, was also bridged by that attacker.

data.title: Altcoins are breaking out, but why isn’t anyone calling it an altseason yet?
data.description:
Altcoins have been stuck in the mud for what feels like forever. However, are things about to change in the near term?

Altcoins have waited two years for THIS!

The combined market cap of every coin outside the top 10 just broke above a trendline it’s been trapped under since late 2024.

And, it’s not been a small move either. In fact, the same is up over 10% this week, starting at about $199 billion to close near $220 billion.

Here, it’s worth noting that all this is happening on a support zone that’s held for about 1,000 days straight.

The timing is interesting too because crypto analyst AshCrypto mentioned on X that the four-year cycle usually treats 2026 as a bear phase. To its credit, Bitcoin’s holding up too, despite the failed Clarity Act vote and the Fed hiking rates.

The altcoins’ all-time high near $451 billion is still a long way off. No one’s calling it altseason yet.

On the other hand…

That’s not all either as at press time, Bitcoin dominance seemed to be forming what looks like a bearish descending triangle on the weekly charts.

If that breaks down, capital might just rotate out of Bitcoin and into everything else. Especially altcoins.

That might even be convenient timing because it would coincide with the breakout alts just noted.

There is a catch here though. CoinShares recently shared that Bitcoin’s stuck between a Fed that’s leaning hawkish and the CLARITY Act’s setback. According to the same, BTC won’t push decisively above $80K before year-end. Not unless inflation calms down or the Fed lowers its tone.

Here, what’s worth noting, however, is that Bitcoin is fairly insulated from the regulatory mess. On the contrary, altcoins like Ethereum [ETH] are far more exposed to it.

What’s holding it back?

For all the breakout talk, one metric refuses to collaborate. CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season Index was at 46 at press time; that’s Bitcoin territory.

It actually climbed up from 42 yesterday and 37 last week. Simply put, the direction is right. Just not the magnitude.

A reading below 75 doesn’t count as an altcoin season by CMC’s own definition. And, the index has been under that mark for months, nowhere near September 2025’s high of 78.

Final Summary

  • Altcoin market cap outside the top 10 broke a 2-year downtrend.
  • BTC.D looked bearish, but the altseason index is still at 46.

data.title: Bitcoin’s bullish phase is forming – But overbought conditions suggest…
data.description:
The crypto market is seeing a major shift in investors’ sentiment. In H2 2027, the digital assets market is experiencing bullish sentiments after failing to break through the long-standing resistance level in H1 2027.

According to CryptoQuant’s recent analysis, Bitcoin [BTC] is moving away from a weakness zone and toward a possible bullish phase. This conclusion was drawn based on Bitcoin’s bubble-versus-crash market structure indicator, which clearly showed that the extreme conditions associated with either a speculative bubble or a severe crash have faded.

Bitcoin has already gone through a period of correction/consolidation, but it has not yet experienced the kind of extreme speculative mania that historically marked major cycle tops. Therefore, the analyst believes BTC could still have room to enter a stronger upward trend.

As per CryptoQuant,

The full-fledged bullish rally has not yet begun. Currently, it is in the process of gradually approaching that stage.

Wall Street bets more on Bitcoin than gold

This comes as JPMorgan sheds light on the fact that institutional investors are more defensively positioned toward Bitcoin than gold. This, along with short interest and put options around Bitcoin ETFs such as BlackRock’s IBIT, now provides more downside protection.

The comparison with gold suggests Bitcoin currently has relatively heavier bearish hedging, while gold ETFs have recovered more of their 2026 outflows. Meanwhile, heavy put-option activity around Bitcoin ETFs indicates investors are protecting against downside. However, this does not necessarily mean they are outright bearish.

In other words, if BTC rallies, these hedges could be unwound, adding further buying pressure. This could in turn lead to a potential market impact of hedge unwinding and short covering worth $1 trillion.

Market dynamics paint a bearish picture

This comes as the price of Bitcoin was changing hands at $78,240.79 at press time after a hike of 2.5% in the past 24 hours. At the same time, the RSI was in the overbought zone, further creating a warning sign that bears might tend to pull the bulls back.

This happened along with the widening Bollinger Bands suggesting that Bitcoin is very volatile at the moment. Adding to the concern was AMBCrypto’s recent report that suggested that crypto’s Q4 outlook is turning cautious as the Fed’s 25 bps rate hike, rising Treasury yields, and a stronger U.S. dollar threaten liquidity and risk assets.

Final Summary

  • The extreme conditions associated with either a speculative bubble or a severe crash around Bitcoin have faded.
  • However, the RSI and Bollinger bands’ RSI suggest that bears might pull the bulls.

data.title: Binance’s MiCA application stalls – ECB President wants Digital Euro ‘fit for future’
data.description:
Binance’s regulatory woes across the European Union (EU) were reportedly driven by political intervention from its central bank, the ECB. 

According to a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report, ECB President Christine Lagarde personally stepped in to block the world’s largest exchange from getting the MiCA license. 

The report claimed that Lagarde ordered Greece to stop the approval process, stating that she “wants the Digital Euro to be fit for the future” and raised concerns over USD-based stablecoins. 

Digital Euro is the ECB’s central bank digital currency (CBDC) and is set for a test pilot from mid-2027, with an official launch scheduled for 2029. However, Lagarde fears that crypto exchanges are driving stablecoin adoption, a move that could undermine the Digital Euro.

But most importantly, Binance’s 2023 guilty plea for money laundering and sanctions violations in the U.S. also played a role in the MiCA license hiccup.

Can Binance secure a MiCA license by 2027?

MiCA’s transitional period ended on the 1st July, 2026. The political intervention forced Binance to withdraw its initial application with Greece’s regulator (HCMC) in mid-June. 

Even so, the exchange maintained that it will reapply for a license from another European country, likely France. Whether it will do so by next year remains unclear. 

Currently, MiCA’s licensing and enforcement are conducted by national authorities, with ESMA (European Securities and Markets Authority) acting as oversight and coordinator. However, from 2027, ESMA will be the sole regulator. 

In fact, the report claimed that there was a push to delay Binance’s approval until ESMA gains sole authority over crypto across the continent. 

Reacting to the update, Binance spokesperson slammed Lagarde’s intervention, stating that MiCA approval shouldn’t be 

A process where applicants can be privately undermined through informal channels.

Other analysts also echoed the same view and wondered whether Europe can apply its rules consistently and fairly. 

Separately, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) wondered why banks are afraid of crypto and blockchains. 

Overall, Binance’s MiCA license hiccup in June was not because it didn’t meet key requirements, at least according to the WSJ report. However, the ECB President sees it as a threat to its Digital Euro vision and chose to temporarily block its approval. 

Final Summary

  • ECB’s Lagarde intervened to stop Binance’s MiCA license approval in Greece, per WSJ
  • Lagarde wants Binance blocked until ESMA gains full MiCA authority and oversight role from national authorities

data.title: Midnight rallies 14% as NIGHT’s bullish fractal returns – Can THIS hold?
data.description:
Midnight [NIGHT] gained 14% over the past day, extending its 30-day return to 36%.

The rally resembled a fractal that had repeatedly shaped NIGHT’s price action during the previous month.

Each move began with a descending resistance breakout before price approached the broader ascending channel’s upper boundary. This time, however, positive Spot inflows introduced selling pressure before the breakout had fully matured.

Can NIGHT hold $0.02277?

The latest move pushed NIGHT above its descending resistance and the $0.02277 horizontal level. The token traded near $0.02331 on the four-hour chart at press time.

However, NIGHT must sustain four-hour closes above $0.02277 to confirm the breakout.

During the previous setup, price rallied above this area before briefly pulling back. A similar move could produce a short-term correction before NIGHT targets the ascending channel’s upper boundary near $0.026.

The fractal favored continuation, but resistance had already triggered one temporary retreat.

Is NIGHT momentum still bullish?

The MACD showed strengthening momentum as its Histogram reached its highest September level. The MACD line rose to 0.00043, remaining above the Signal line at 0.00009.

Meanwhile, the MACD Histogram increased to 0.00034, showing that bullish momentum continued expanding.

The Accumulation/Distribution also improved to -22.77 billion from below -22.8 billion.

Although the reading remained negative, its recovery suggested that buying activity had strengthened since the 15th of September. Continued improvement could support NIGHT during any retest of the reclaimed resistance.

Will spot inflows trigger a pullback?

Spot activity presented the main challenge to NIGHT’s bullish technical structure. CoinGlass recorded $512,250 in five-day Net Inflow and $367,260 over 24 hours.

Positive Net Inflow meant more NIGHT entered exchanges than left them, increasing the supply available for selling. Continued inflows could trigger the temporary pullback projected by the fractal.

However, a successful $0.02277 retest could turn that correction into another stage of the broader rally. The pattern has repeated before. Its next test is whether traders anticipating it begin changing its outcome.

Final Summary

  • NIGHT price rose 14% over 24 hours and 36% across 30 days.
  • Midnight broke above descending resistance and the key $0.02277 horizontal level.

data.title: Crypto treasury stocks face $50B loss as shareholders revolt – What happened?
data.description:
Investors who hopped into last year’s crypto boom are now turning up the pressure on digital-asset treasury (DAT) firms. In fact, both retail and institutional shareholders are now demanding greater accountability after losses across the sector reached roughly $50 billion.

According to Bloomberg, investors initially bought their shares because they expected the companies’ crypto holdings to rise in value. Along with this, they also expected that the stocks could sometimes trade at a premium to the value of the crypto they owned.

However, now that crypto prices and these stocks have fallen sharply, shareholders are questioning whether management is using their money effectively.

How an year changed the course of things?

In this shift, retail investors are becoming more vocal online, while institutional investors are pushing for changes through shareholder votes, takeover proposals, and challenges to compensation plans.

Here it’s important to note that the roughly $50 billion in cumulative losses mentioned is actually the decline in the value of these publicly traded treasury companies. And not $50 billion that shareholders necessarily lost in one particular event.

In this, the concerning part according to Artemis is that publicly listed DATs whose main treasury strategy focused on Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] have a combined fully diluted market value of around $90 billion. In other words, it’s now about 40% below the sector’s previous peak.

Shockingly, this figure excludes companies whose main treasury strategy revolves around smaller altcoins such as Solana [SOL].

Solana DAT’s downfall

Yet despite the exclusion, Sky AI, formerly Sharps Technology, is a key example of the growing scrutiny around crypto treasury firms. After raising more than $400 million to build a Solana treasury, its stock has now fallen nearly 90% since August 2025.

Forward Industries, another Solana DAT, previously attempted to acquire SkyAI and is now opposing its proposed 7.2% equity allocation for about 30 employees, worth roughly $4 million at current prices.

Additionally, Investors are also questioning Sky AI’s warrants, including those granted to a strategic advisor with an estimated $101.3 million accounting fair value.

Bitcoin: Strategy’s good luck

That said, Metaplanet faced similar backlash after its stock fell about 84% from its June 2025 peak, with retail investors criticizing its incentive structure and potential dilution from warrants. This comes after the company subsequently canceled certain warrants reportedly worth around $220 million.

While all this was happening, Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which also lost its momentum a while back, saw a completely different ball game. Recently, the largest BTC DAT repurchased $139 million of STRC preferred stock. This pushed its Bitcoin holdings to reach 845,050 BTC, worth $65.83 billion, alongside $6.4 billion in USD assets, strengthening its liquidity position.

Final Summary

  • $50 billion in cumulative losses is actually the decline in the value of these publicly traded treasury companies.
  • Companies whose main treasury strategy did not revolve just around Bitcoin and Ethereum also faced similar downfalls.
